new.n: English officer's buried bullion, New Baltimore
new.pl: New Baltimore (city), Macomb Co; the story says about a mile from the 1882 village, direction not given
new.st: The 1882 county history records a tradition, 'with many believers even now', that an English captain or lieutenant carrying 'a quantity of bullion', fleeing Indians, 'buried his treasure in the earth about a mile from the present site of New Baltimore'; he died and the secret died with him. There were many searches, and a ghost is said to guard and move it. The passage sits under Tremble Creek (Marsac's c.1798 settlement on the Ridge road) and Swan Creek. Pin is the town only, not the spot.
new.t: Legend only; a mile ring around a now-built-up town. Look for the Tremble Creek / Ridge Road side first. Access: private/urban.
src: Leeson, History of Macomb County, Michigan (1882), pp. 484-485
pinev: New Baltimore city point; the story gives 'about a mile' from the 1882 village with no direction, so r2000.

new.n: Vansickle counterfeiters' cabin, S½ sec 31 Ovid Twp
new.pl: S½ sec 31 T7N R1W, Ovid Twp, Clinton Co (1880 county history)
new.st: The 1880 county history says that in summer 1838 William Vansickle cleared and built a cabin on the south half of section 31, Ovid Twp. A Detroit posse, tipped by Henry Leach of Sciota, caught Vansickle, a woman, and Ward, Skiff and Gridley making counterfeit Mexican dollars; Vansickle had carried the coin to Detroit in a black valise. Pin is the half-section centre, not the cabin.
new.t: Coin dies and bogus Mexican dollars are the targets; an 1838 cabin site in a half-section. Check the 1873/1896 Clinton plats for the owner. Access: private farmland.
src: History of Shiawassee and Clinton Counties, Michigan (1880), Ovid Twp chapter
pinev: S½ sec 31 T7N R1W centre from BLM PLSS (sec 31 box 42.9428-42.9573 / -84.4837 to -84.4641); r600.

new.n: Counterfeiters' block-house ('Old House'), Manistee River sec 36
new.pl: Sec 36 T22N R14W on the Manistee River; the block-house stood on the river bank inside the section
new.st: The 1882 county history says Massachusetts men built a strong block-house up the Manistee River in sec 36 T22N R14W before 1849 (Indians stopped their dam); 'at a very early day this old block-house was taken possession of by a gang of counterfeiters' who made bogus dollars there. It stood 'until a few years ago' (c.1880). Pin is the section centre, not the block-house.
new.t: A pre-1849 block-house site on the river bank; coin dies and bogus dollars possible. Lidar may show the cellar or dam cut. Access: mixed state forest/private.
src: Page, History of Manistee County, Michigan (1882)
pinev: Sec 36 T22N R14W centre from BLM PLSS (box 44.2528-44.2675 / -85.9617 to -85.9414), Dickson Twp near High Bridge; r800.

new.n: Bogus Island counterfeiters, Fox River above Algonquin
new.pl: Fox River island about 1 mi upstream of Algonquin; not named on modern maps
new.st: The 1885 McHenry county history says counterfeiters frequenting Algonquin village 'were finally tracked to Bogus Island, about a mile further up the stream, where they were captured'; it was Allan Pinkerton's first detective case. The 1878 Kane County history tells Pinkerton's capture of 'Old Craig' (taken to Geneva), likely the same affair. Pin is about a mile up the Fox River from Algonquin, not the island itself.
new.t: Coin dies and bogus coin on a river island; the island may be gone or joined to the bank. Access: river/parkland, look-only.
src: History of McHenry County, Illinois (1885), p. 389
History of Kane County, Illinois (1878), p. 230
pinev: About 1 mi upstream (N) of Algonquin on the Fox River; island not named on modern maps; r800.
